## The sum of a geometric series {#ss6-formulas .gs-lesson .gs-formulas}

::: {.split .gs-formula-layout}

::: {.column-block}

$$S_n=\frac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}\qquad(r\ne1)$$

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}

Multiply the numerator and denominator by $-1$:

$$S_n=\frac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}\qquad(r\ne1)$$

:::


::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}

Both forms give the same sum.

$a$: first term being added<br>
$n$: number of terms being added

:::

:::

::: notes


This completes Example 6.2(d) and the result box. First click shows the equivalent form with r−1 in the denominator. Second click stresses the meaning of a and n. Either formula works for every permitted ratio; choosing by whether r is above or below 1 is a convenience, not a restriction. For a sum with a non-1 lower index, a means the first INCLUDED term and n counts the terms included. The image is the teacher-supplied screenshot from 20 October 2026, copied unchanged with its existing red outline. Do not teach its limiting-sum formula yet.
